ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First look at the image: the vertex of the protractor is at B, the left end O of the base is marked 0°, and the right end is marked 180°; ray BD points to the upper right and aligns with the position of about 160° on the right side; ray BA points to the upper left, close to the 20° mark on the left side, but it is not directly using the “20” number printed in the figure as an exact scale mark, rather it is slightly above the position near that mark, and according to the approximate reading of the protractor it can be taken as about 30°; ray BC points more steeply to the upper left and is between BA and BD. The problem gives that ∠CBD is a right angle, so the protractor readings of BC and BD differ by 90°. From BD being about 160°, BC can be obtained as about 160°−90°=70°. Therefore ∠ABC is approximately equal to the difference between the readings of BC and BA: 70°−30°≈40°, so the answer is about 40°.

raw_record.question_text: If $\angle\text{CBD}$ is a right angle, what is the approximate measure of $\angle\text{ABC}$ indicated by this protractor?

method.method_draft: Read the protractor scale directly: in the image, the vertex is B, ray BD lines up with about 160° on the protractor, and ray BA lines up at about 30°. The text states that ∠CBD is a right angle, so ray BC must be 90° away from BD. Since C lies between A and D on the protractor, subtract 90° from D’s 160° reading to place C at about 70°. Then compute ∠ABC as the difference between the C and A readings: 70° − 30° ≈ 40°.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: If $\angle\text{CBD}$ is a right angle, what is the approximate measure of $\angle\text{ABC}$ indicated by this protractor?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: If $\angle\text{CBD}$ is a right angle, what is the approximate measure of $\angle\text{ABC}$ indicated by this protractor?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: First look at the image: the vertex of the protractor is at B, the left end O of the base is marked 0°, and the right end is marked 180°; ray BD points to the upper right and aligns with the position of about 160° on the right side; ray BA points to the upper left, close to the 20° mark on the left side, but it is not directly using the “20” number printed in the figure as an exact scale mark, rather it is slightly above the position near that mark, and according to the approximate reading of the protractor it can be taken as about 30°; ray BC points more steeply to the upper left and is between BA and BD. The problem gives that ∠CBD is a right angle, so the protractor readings of BC and BD differ by 90°. From BD being about 160°, BC can be obtained as about 160°−90°=70°. Therefore ∠ABC is approximately equal to the difference between the readings of BC and BA: 70°−30°≈40°, so the answer is about 40°.
